concept: SQL Server resumable index operations: ELEVATE_RESUMABLE and resumable constraints
summary: Source-anchored research for SQL Server resumable index operations: ELEVATE_RESUMABLE and resumable constraints. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: ELEVATE_RESUMABLE is a database-scoped default available from SQL Server 2019: OFF is the default, WHEN_SUPPORTED elevates eligible operations and lets unsupported ones run nonresumably, and FAIL_UNSUPPORTED rejects unsupported execution within its scope. Configure it with ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET ELEVATE_RESUMABLE = WHEN_SUPPORTED. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-20)

ELEVATE_RESUMABLE affects only DDL supporting RESUMABLE syntax when the statement omits that option. Explicit RESUMABLE = OFF overrides even FAIL_UNSUPPORTED; XML index operations are outside the setting. Treat this as a default, not an unconditional enforcement policy. (high confidence)

Database defaults can make eligible index DDL resumable without an explicit RESUMABLE clause. Brent Ozar demonstrates why callers must account for retained paused work when cancelling such DDL. (medium confidence)
Enable resumable constraint creation with WITH (ONLINE = ON, RESUMABLE = ON). MAX_DURATION specifies minutes until automatic pause; if omitted, execution continues to completion. (high confidence)

Microsoft's constraint documentation shows manual PAUSE disconnecting the original session with error 1219, followed by error 1750, while the operation remains PAUSED in sys.index_resumable_operations. (low confidence)

A failed constraint build can remain paused. MSSQLTips demonstrates a duplicate-key failure followed by error 10637 on attempted constraint removal; inspect sys.index_resumable_operations and explicitly ABORT work that should be discarded. (medium confidence)
Resumable constraint creation can continue after maintenance-window pauses, failovers or system failures rather than restarting all work. (medium confidence)

ELEVATE_RESUMABLE is documented for SQL Server 2019 and later, Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance; it supplies a database-scoped resumable default for eligible DDL. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-06)

SQL Server 2022 adds resumable ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT for PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints, excluding FOREIGN KEY constraints; execution requires ONLINE = ON. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-18)
Manage resumable constraint creation with ALTER INDEX ALL ON <table> PAUSE, RESUME or ABORT; inspect progress using sys.index_resumable_operations. (high confidence)

AWS announced that Amazon RDS for SQL Server 2022 supports pausing and resuming ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT, including recovery after failovers or system failures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-11-16)
Microsoft requires ALTER permission on the table and specifies no new permission for resumable ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT. (low confidence)

The database-scoped configuration reference documents PAUSED_RESUMABLE_INDEX_ABORT_DURATION_MINUTES with a 1,440-minute default and zero disabling automatic abort; verify platform support and actual configuration before assuming indefinite retention. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-06)

Monitor constraint creation through sys.index_resumable_operations using sql_text, state_desc and percent_complete. The catalog documents total_execution_time in minutes and state values 0 for running and 1 for paused. (high confidence)
